To: Operations and Logistics Leadership  
From: Supply Chain Director  
Date: Today  
Subject: Cost-effective shipping plan across our multi-node network

Situation
We operate a broad network of warehouses and plants serving a large set of stores and customers. Freight rates and handling charges vary by route, and some locations face tighter inventory availability than others. To protect service levels and control logistics spend, we need a clear, executable shipping plan that aligns supply with demand across the network. Partial shipments are allowed, so destinations can be served from more than one source and loads can be split as needed.

Problem
We must determine how much to ship from each source to each destination so that every destination’s requirement is fully met without exceeding available inventory or capacity at any source, while keeping total transportation spend as low as possible. The challenge is to balance limited supply, uneven demand, and route-specific costs, leveraging lower-cost lanes where practical without compromising on-time delivery.

Approach
We will consolidate three inputs: available-to-ship quantities at each source, required quantities at each destination, and per-route shipping costs. Using our planning tools, we will produce a feasible allocation that meets all requirements, respects source limits, and achieves the lowest total shipping cost practical. The output will include lane-by-lane shipment recommendations and a projected spend summary for review and execution. We will refresh the plan as supply, demand, or rate assumptions change to ensure continued cost efficiency and service reliability.
